title: Physical Synthesis Optimization Prediction Using Machine Learning
problem: Long EDA tool runtimes act as bottlenecks for design turn-around-time in complex SOC design implementation, requiring designers to wait for complete tool runs to obtain critical Power-Performance-Area (PPA) parameters such as timing slack, critical path depth, leakage power, and area.
motivation: Early availability of estimated PPA parameters before or parallel to actual tool-based runs can significantly accelerate design convergence and improve engineering productivity in iterative design flows.
method: The approach trains a machine learning model on real data from thousands of previous chip designs at sub-10nm scale (an extremely advanced manufacturing process), typically running at 1 GHz clock speeds. The model learns to predict the final power consumption, speed, and physical area of a new chip directly from intermediate design data—avoiding the need to run complete engineering tool simulations. With 6-10% accuracy, this early prediction can happen in parallel with other design work or even before the simulation tools start.
key_novelty: Machine learning trained on past chip designs can directly predict a new chip's power consumption, performance, and area early in the process with 6-10% accuracy, eliminating the need to wait for slow tool simulations.
contributions: ML-based framework for early PPA prediction in physical synthesis
Prediction model for timing slack and critical path depth
Leakage power and area estimation within 6-10% accuracy
Validation on sub-10nm SOC designs at 1 GHz operation
limitations: Abstract only; accuracy baseline of 6-10% suggests room for improvement; limited details on dataset size and diversity.
